recipes.name: Super Easy Rosemary Bread Machine Bread
ingredients_raw: 1 cup warm water (110 degrees F (43 degrees C))

steps.text: Pour the water into the pan of a bread machine, then sprinkle in the yeast and sugar. Let the mixture sit in the bread machine until a creamy foam forms on top of the water, about 10 minutes. Sprinkle in the salt, then add olive oil, thyme, garlic powder, rosemary, and flour. Set the machine for light crust setting, and start the machine.

raw_recipe.headline: Super Easy Rosemary Bread Machine Bread
raw_recipe.description: A light and fluffy herb bread is easy to make in the machine, and uses no eggs, milk, or butter.
raw_recipe.name: Super Easy Rosemary Bread Machine Bread

review.reviewBody: Oh my, this is the best white bread to come out of my bread machine in a long time. I followed the recipe exactly, but put the ingredients into the pan in the order recommended by the manufacturer of my machine, NOT in the order listed here. I used bread machine yeast, so did not proof the yeast in the water; I added the water and oil, then the flour, then the spices, salt, and sugar around the edge, and put the yeast in a little crater in the middle. My machine makes 2-3 lb loaves so I set in on white, two pound, light crust, and it rose up so fluffy and perfect. Great sandwich bread too! I've printed this recipe and can't wait to make more.

Wow! This is absolutely delicious! Easy to make, and thank goodness because it disappears so fast in this household! I decreased the flour to 3 cups (Bob's Red Mill Artisan Bread Flour), increased the oil by about a teaspoon, and increased the crushed rosemary to a well-rounded tablespoon. The texture is soft and chewy with a lightly crispy crust. (Breadman Bread Machine, light crust setting). This bread is perfect for dipping into olive oil, or toasted with butter and honey or jam...or just sliced and eaten. I highly recommend this recipe!

We loved it... though used 1 TBSP fresh rosemary and I decided to leave out the garlic and thyme, and only used 2 TBSP sugar. I used the dough setting. Shaped into two loaves and rose again for about 45 minutes. Baked for about 30 minutes. Came out soft and fluffy with a slight crust. very nice.

This is a wonderful recipe! I've tried the original, then tried doubling the herbs. Both turned out great (but we did prefer the doubled herb batch). Yesterday I used this recipe to create a light rye bread by changing the 3 C white flour to 1 cup each white, whole wheat & rye flours - also dropped the herbs but adding 1 Tbls caraway and ground flax seed. EXCELLENTLY AWESOME RESULTS!!! - In each case, I used my bread machine to only mix the dough, baking the loaf in my oven. As suggested by others, I followed my bread machine directions with regard to the placement of the yeast (not premixing it). - I'm thinking that I won't be buying 'store-bought' bread very much anymore - so THANK YOU STACY!

This bread was AMAZING! Very light texture, fantastic flavor. I added the ingredients in the order of my machine directions, so water, oil, flour and then the dry seasoning with the yeast in the little well in the middle. I'm not a huge garlic fan, so I decreased the garlic powder to 1/4 tsp, and upped the rosemary to 2 tablespoons. I also added about a tablespoon of fresh basil. Set machine to basic, 2lb, medium crust. I will ABSOLUTELY be making this break again. My family devoured it immediately!!

I pulled out my 20 year old bread machine for this recipe. The max baking time on my machine was 2:40 so I had to figure out how to add time to get the bread completely done. I added 40 minutes which made the bread come out a bit crustier but that was actually great! And my family LOVED it. I will make this super easy recipe over and over.

Easy recipe - great results! I did double up on the thyme and rosemary as we like our bread really "herby." We have a Mr. Coffee BreadMaker extra lrg 2 lb. capacity and we made this on setting 3 for light crust. This bread, combined with a good quality olive oil, makes an excellent appetizer. I plan on making this frequently!

Made this for a ladies summer dinner, turned out fabulous! I substituted 1 cup whole wheat flour for 1 cup of white bread flour and it worked great. I did think it a bit too sweet, 3 tablespoons of sugar is a lot, next time I will try two. Also I followed one of the other reviews and put items in liquids first, then flour, seasonings, sugar and bread yeast in the well last. I was a bit concerned because my yeast was a week past use date (it is kept in frig) but it was just fine. Highly recommend! 
Served with a cream cheese spread of parsley with lemon. Yum!

I love this recipe. I have been making it for years. I have tried it according to standard bread machine directions as well as the directions on the recipe and it was always hit and miss. I found the most consistent way to make it is by proofing the yeast first in the pan and always testing the water temperature with a thermometer. Also making sure to let the yeast proof for a full 10 minutes and it should be thick ,foamy and bubbling, If it isn't start over with the yeast. 

I also add an extra 2 cloves of fresh garlic, extra fresh rosemary if I have it and a little extra olive oil. You can smell the garlic and olive oil as it's baking and it is heavenly.

You can use all purpose flour or bread flour, I prefer a combination of both but it's great either way. You can also use this as a basic bread recipe and make variations like, olive bread or parmesan cheese bread. 

A great crowd pleaser!
Excellent! I made a couple of changes to the recipe. I used Molasses instead of sugar, fresh garlic, and sundried tomato infused olive oil. It turned out so light and delicious

Holy cow!! Like another reviewer, I changed up the order of ingredients. I have an Oster bread machine and followed their recommendation of liquid then solids then yeast. Set it to the "Basic Bread: Large" setting. It came out amazing! It's still cooling so hopefully it stiffens up a little for sandwiches (it's a soft as a cloud right now), but it's AMAZING with some butter right now!! Bookmarking. Not sure if it would have worked with doing the water and yeast first, but definitely worked by following the bread machine instructions. Thanks!!!
This recipe was ok, but a little heavy on the rosemary. I prefer the basic recipe I usually make.
Reliable! I live at altitude (+6550ft), so added a bit more liquid. The family prefers this to store-bought bread for sandwiches, and is so much more affordable!

This recipe is PERFECTION! I’ve been using your recipe for over 10 years now, and it’s the bread requested and family gatherings! I did take the advice of one commenter from 2011 who said to add ingredients in the order your specific machine instructs, and that has served me well! Two thumbs up!

Easy and tasty. I'm high-altitude so I used 1 packet of yeast, which is 1/4 tsp less than the recipe, plus slightly less sugar and a tad more water. Rose beautifully. Kid doesn't like the aftertaste of the garlic.

I used bread flour (3 parts high gluten flour and 1 part regular flour), seasoning salt, and added fresh basil, and slightly more oil. Next time I will add more seasoning. I like more flavor in my bread. But It came out super fluffy and perfectly brown. My BF loved it! I am saving this recipe and using it again.

Used fresh rosemary and thyme because that's what I had. Used Tuscan Infused Olive Oil from The Olive Oiler in downtown Fort Worth. Absolutely scrumptious hot out of the machine with extra olive oil and basalmic vinegar for dipping or slathered in butter!

Made this on vacay at a friends house who had never used her bread maker...so easy...she was so impressed and her n hubby loved loved loved the bread as did i! We dug into it on a car trip right after i has made it...both thought it was sooooo good! Ty! Gonna make again today n gonna try adding some parmesan cheese!

This bread was delicious and so easy. I used bread flour and followed the usual order for putting in the ingredients. I combined the dried herbs and salt to a small dish, crushed them and added them together. Then, I put the sugar around the edge. Lastly, I dug a little “well” for the yeast in the center. It works nicely.
I used 1 Tablespoon fresh rosemary since I had fresh(another review did this). My bread basket for the bread machine didn’t release the bread so the bottom tore…will spray the bottom next time
